bhajan.title: Amrutha Sai Naama Akhanda Sai Prema

discourse.excerpt: The person who serves is the person served; you serve yourself when you serve another. You serve another because his suffering causes you anguish and by relieving it, you want to save yourselves from that anguish.
discourse.theme: Service becomes saadhana only when filled with prema — the server and the served are one.
discourse.title: Seva as saadhana

reflection: Swami is honest about why service sometimes leaves everyone frustrated: without prema it is hollow. His remedy — fill every act of service with unselfish love, and receive service with the eye of prema too. The person who serves is the person served. Before your next act of help, pause and let your heart feel the other person's need as your own; then serve. That is seva as saadhana. (Sri Sathya Sai Speaks, Vol 7, 6 Nov 1967)
seva_nudge: Do one quiet act of service today — tidy the bhajan hall, help an elder with their groceries, wash dishes at the center — and keep it between you and Swami.
